record.summary: Voluntary framework of Singapore's Personal Data Protection Commission for organisations deploying AI at scale, in any sector and regardless of technology or algorithm. It turns common AI ethics principles into practices in four areas: internal governance structures and measures; the level of human involvement in AI-augmented decisions, set with a matrix of the probability and severity of harm (human-in-the-loop, over-the-loop or out-of-the-loop); operations management, covering data, explainability, repeatability, robustness, traceability, reproducibility and auditability; and stakeholder interaction and communication.
record.notes: The first edition was released on 23 Jan 2019 and the second on 21 Jan 2020, both at the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos. The second edition added industry examples, clarified the human-over-the-loop approach, added robustness, reproducibility and auditability measures, replaced the use-case annex with a separate Compendium of Use Cases and limited algorithm audits to a regulator's request. IMDA and the PDPC developed a companion Implementation and Self-Assessment Guide for Organisations (ISAGO) with the World Economic Forum. Under the Personal Data Protection Act 2012, the IMDA is designated as the PDPC.

legal_force.quote: This voluntary Model Framework provides guidance on the key issues to be considered and measures that can be implemented.
The contents herein are not intended to be an authoritative statement of the law or a substitute for legal or other professional advice.

summary.quote: The Model Framework focuses primarily on four broad areas: internal governance structures and measures, human involvement in AI-augmented decision-making, operations management and stakeholder interaction and communication.
It serves as a baseline set of considerations and measures for organisations operating in any sector to adopt.
as a general, ready-to-use tool to enable organisations that are deploying AI solutions at scale to do so in a responsible manner.
The Model Framework uses existing and common AI ethical principles (a compilation of which is set out in Annex A) and converts them into implementable practices.
This design framework is structured along two axes: the (a) probability; and (b) severity of harm to an individual (or organisation)
Human-over-the-loop (or human-on-the-loop) suggests that human oversight is involved to the extent that the human is in a monitoring or supervisory role
Measures such as explainability, repeatability, robustness, regular tuning, reproducibility, traceability, and auditability can enhance the transparency of algorithms found in AI models.

notes.quote: FIRST 23 January 2019 Released the Model AI Governance Framework (First Edition) at the 2019 World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos, Switzerland.
